prompt: A speaker makes a tone modelled by $y = 2\sin(9x)$, where $x$ is in degrees. How many degrees long is ONE full wave?
hint: One full wave is the PERIOD, and period $= 360^\circ \div b$.

hints.text: One full wave is the PERIOD, and period $= 360^\circ \div b$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $y = 2\sin(3x)$: the period is $360 \div 3 = 120^\circ$. Now use the same division with $b = 9$.

explanation: For $y = a\sin(bx)$, the period is $360^\circ \div b$.
The $2$ out front is the amplitude — how LOUD the tone is — and it does not change the length of a wave.
$360 \div 9 = 40^\circ$. A bigger $b$ packs the waves tighter, which is what a higher pitch sounds like.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count the waves in one turn
steps: b = 9 means 9 complete waves are squeezed into a 360° stretch.

alternativeExplanations.title: Follow the inside
steps: A wave is finished when the inside of the sine has gone from 0 up to 360.
The inside is 9x, so set 9x = 360. Dividing gives x = 40, so the x-trip is 40°.
